name: Mai Chau
provinceNote: Xã Mai Châu has been in Phú Thọ since the 2025 merger (Resolution 202/2025/QH15 and Resolution 1676/NQ-UBTVQH15, governments from 1 July 2025).
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: A green valley of rice fields and Thai stilt-house villages, a short trip west of Hanoi. Sleep in a homestay in Ban Lac or Pom Coong, walk through the fields, and eat bamboo-tube rice and hill chicken at the family table. One night suits families and anyone wanting countryside close to the capital.
timeNeeded: A night and the next morning

seoTitle: Mai Chau travel guide — rice valley, White Thai houses, cycling
seoDescription: Cycle the paths between White Thai stilt houses and the rice, and sleep in a house in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng. October is one golden window.
intro: You cycle the paths between White Thai stilt houses and the rice, with Bản Lác and Pom Coọng on the valley floor and the limestone ridge behind. The night is a house there, the fields at the edge. Stay if that valley morning is the trip. Pù Luông is the trek from this valley, a full day, and a half day is too short for it. Mộc Châu is the next highland on the same highway, past this valley, and it is its own night.

Give the quiet hour of the morning to the lanes. Have cà phê phin looking at the rice, then take a bicycle between the houses and the paddies. Weaving sits in front of the houses and under the floors. The Sunday morning market is the morning people come in formal dress and the cloth is sold. Electric carts are the other way between villages.

The evening is the stilt-house floor. After dinner, White Thai music and dance. In Pom Coọng the programme is xòe, sạp, and instruments. Khắp Thái is part of the evening exchange. Travelers fall asleep early under countryside dark. Bản Lác holds a cultural night market on Saturday evening, in xã Mai Hạ. Pà Cò’s Sunday morning market, and the Saturday night market at Bản Chà Đáy, are the highland markets, a different morning from the valley’s Sunday market.

Hang Kia and Pà Cò are the Hmong highland of this stay, now xã Pà Cò, on National Highway 6 toward Sơn La, then about 6 km between Bản Chà Đáy and Hang Kia village. Bản Chà Đáy sits at 1,140 m. Spring brings plum and peach, and a cloud sea. The high point named with the reserve is 1,536 m, a different figure from the village.

The caves are a thinner visit than the rice. Hang Piềng Kẻm is a national scenic site by Decision 39/2005/QĐ-BVHTT of 22 August 2005, then in xã Chiềng Châu, now inside xã Mai Hạ. Hang Chiều is one of the national-level relics, with a repair planned for 2026–2030. Hang Nà Lằn, at xóm Chà Đáy, is the cave for late in the day, when sun comes through the mouth. Hang Khoài is named with it, at xóm Bin. Dinner is the house. The plates are on the food guide.
gettingAround: The usual start is Hanoi. No Mai Châu airfield is named. Nội Bài is the airport, then the road through Hòa Bình and National Highway 6. No Mai Châu station is named. Ga Hà Nội is at 120 Lê Duẩn.

A bus leaves from Mỹ Đình, and a shuttle, a private car, or a motorbike are the other ways. Local buses run to Mai Châu town, a short walk from Bản Lác and Pom Coọng. A traveler from Sơn La or Điện Biên should ask the driver to stop at the Mai Châu turn-off. The morning is the better time to drive, for the view at đèo Thung Khe.

On the valley floor the bicycle is the way between the stilt houses and the paddies. Bicycle hire is 20.000–50.000 đồng a trip. Núi Đầu Rồng is the viewpoint for the whole valley, early-morning mist and afternoon cloud. June to August monsoon can flood local roads, and heavier rain also runs from May to September.

stayAreas.name: Ban Lac
stayAreas.summary: The main cluster of White Thai stilt houses, on the flat lanes between the roofs and the paddies. The village is more than 700 years old, with foreign guests from the 1960s. Bản Lác sits in xã Mai Hạ, formed from Chiềng Châu, Vạn Mai, and Mai Hạ. Older listings place it in xã Chiềng Châu. The town bus drop is a short walk. A rustic homestay is about 200.000 đồng, a boutique farm stay about 600.000 đồng, and a four-star hotel about 1.500.000 đồng.

stayAreas.name: Pom Coong
stayAreas.summary: The second White Thai village, quieter than the main homestay cluster, in the center of xã Mai Châu. It was also placed in the township. The name is hill plus drum. About 70 households and more than 300 people. Houses of bamboo, wood, or bương stand about 2 m off the ground, with weaving under the floor. Sleep here when you want the same valley and a smaller lane. The commune counts 45 community homestays, 15 guesthouses, and 3 hotels. A 2022 count of the old district is more than 200 lodging businesses. The geography and the year differ.

eat: Dinner is the homestay table in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng: cơm lam from the bamboo tube, gà đồi, pork skewers, xôi nếp, and rượu cần. Bản Hịch, about 12 km from the old district center, serves vịt đầu xanh, rau sắng, and cá dầm xanh. Hang Kia serves xôi nếp nương, lợn bản, gà nướng, and bánh dày. The list is on the food guide.
interestsBody: The night is a rice valley and a stilt-house floor, closer to Hanoi than the high terraces. Dinner is that house. Weaving is under the floor and at the Sunday market. The bicycle is the way across the paddies.

body: The meal is the house in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng: cơm lam, gà đồi, thịt lợn xiên nướng, stuffed fried cicadas, vịt cỏ, lợn cắp nách, lợn mán, gà nướng, dế nướng, xôi nếp, rượu cần, rượu Mai Hạ, nhộng ong rừng, and măng chua. Bản Hịch, about 12 km from the old district center, serves vịt đầu xanh, rau sắng, and cá dầm xanh. Hang Kia serves xôi nếp nương, lợn bản, gà nướng, and bánh dày. The table also includes cá suối, cá suối chiên, canh cải mèo, trâu gác bếp, and chẩm chéo.

body: Bản Lác is the main homestay lane. Pom Coọng is the quieter village in the center of xã Mai Châu, a short walk or a bicycle from the town bus drop. Bản Văn is the next hamlet on that walk, with stilt rows and a wider green. Nà Phòn is a Thai community village inside xã Mai Châu.
Bicycle hire is 20.000–50.000 đồng a trip. The paths run between the houses and the paddies. A motorbike is the road from Hanoi, and the bicycle is the way across the floor.

blocks.heading: Hang Kia and Pa Co
paragraphs: This is the Hmong highland of the same stay, now xã Pà Cò, formed from Cun Pheo, Hang Kia, Pà Cò, and the rest of Đồng Tân. The road is National Highway 6 toward Sơn La, then about 6 km from Bản Chà Đáy to Hang Kia village. Bản Chà Đáy is at 1,140 m. The Saturday night market is there, and the Pà Cò market is Sunday morning. Spring plum and peach, a cloud sea, and Hmong weaving and dyeing are the season, with no fixed civil dates. A waterfall near the Pà Cò community village is named separately from thác Gò Lào.

blocks.heading: Caves in the valley hills
paragraphs: Hang Piềng Kẻm is a national scenic site by Decision 39/2005/QĐ-BVHTT of 22 August 2005. Hang Chiều and Hang Láng are named with Hang Mỏ Luông. Hang Nà Lằn is the late-afternoon cave, for sun through the mouth, at xóm Chà Đáy. Hang Khoài is at xóm Bin.

blocks.heading: A family night on the floor
paragraphs: One night in the house, a bicycle in the morning, and an early dark. After dinner the floor is White Thai music and dance, xòe and sạp in Pom Coọng, and khắp Thái in the evening exchange. Keng Loóng, the pestle dance on a wooden trough, is national intangible heritage of the Thai in this district, performed at Xên Mường and at the evening exchange.

Xên Mường is annual in the first lunar month, on the 9th and 10th. The 2026 opening was 26 February, the 10th, in xã Mai Hạ. A 2024 reception was 19 February, also the 10th, at the Tướng Sứ shrine in xóm Chiềng Châu. The civil date moves with the moon. Offerings named in 2026 include buffalo, pigs, chickens, sticky rice, wine, and two decorated buffaloes. Xên bản, lễ mừng cơm mới, lễ Chá chiêng, and the Hmong Gầu Tào are named rites.

interestGroups.summary: Sunday morning cloth in the valley, the Saturday night market at Bản Lác, and the highland markets at Pà Cò and Bản Chà Đáy.

blocks.heading: Sunday morning cloth
paragraphs: The Sunday morning market is the morning people come in formal dress and woven cloth is sold. Weaving also sits under the stilt houses and in the lanes. It is a different market from Pà Cò. Rượu ngô, tỏi tía, and a sâm planting at Chà Đáy are products of the commune.

blocks.heading: Ban Lac Saturday night
paragraphs: A cultural night market runs at Bản Lác, in xã Mai Hạ, on Saturday evening, under the same stilt houses you sleep in.

blocks.heading: Pa Co and Ban Cha Day
paragraphs: The Pà Cò market meets on Sunday morning. Bản Chà Đáy holds a night market on Saturday evening. The highland is on National Highway 6 toward Sơn La, about 6 km on from Bản Chà Đáy to Hang Kia village.

cards.summary: Woven cloth on Sunday morning, and weaving under the stilt houses through the week.

faqs.q: Should you stay in Mai Chau, Pu Luong, or Moc Chau?
faqs.a: Stay in Mai Chau when the morning is a rice valley, a White Thai stilt house, and a bicycle between the paddies, about 140 km from Hanoi. Ride to Pù Luông when you want the full-day trek. Continue to Mộc Châu when the tea plateau past the pass is the night you booked.

faqs.q: How long is the road from Hanoi?
faqs.a: About 140 km, and also about 150 km, 130 km from central Hanoi, and 157 km from Nội Bài. Allow about three hours by car or bus via Hòa Bình, and also 2.5 hours. The bus leaves from Mỹ Đình.

In a stilt house in Bản Lác or Pom Coọng. Bản Lác is the main cluster, in xã Mai Hạ, and older listings place it in xã Chiềng Châu. Pom Coọng is quieter, in the center of xã Mai Châu, with about 70 households. A rustic homestay is about 200.000 đồng, a boutique farm stay about 600.000 đồng, and a four-star hotel about 1.500.000 đồng. The commune counts 45 community homestays, 15 guesthouses, and 3 hotels. A 2022 count of the old district is more than 200 lodging businesses.

September to November is the harvest, with October the golden month, and March to May the other pleasant window. The rice also starts to turn gold in late May and early June, and is gold again in September and October. Heavier rain runs from May to September, and June to August monsoon can flood local roads.

Annual in the first lunar month, on the 9th and 10th. In 2026 the opening was 26 February, the 10th, in xã Mai Hạ. The 2024 reception was 19 February, also the 10th. The civil date moves with the moon.
